findings.finding: Designation-only actions are the weakest instrument
findings.evidence: Garantex 2022: volume doubled post-designation; Bitpapa: triple-designated, still operating; Stark: evaded EU sanctions before they took effect; Media Land: shells pre-built before designation
findings.implication: Never lead with sanctions alone; sequence designations with seizures, freezes or arrests, and designate evasion shells at birth (Nov 2025 OFAC model)

findings.finding: Arrests plus attribution outperform infrastructure seizure
findings.evidence: Score-5 actions all include custody (Phobos Aetor, Cryptex, UK retail cluster); DanaBot stayed dead on naming alone; LummaC2 (no arrests) recovered in weeks
findings.implication: Prioritize actions with a custody or full-attribution component; indictment naming has independent suppressive value

findings.finding: Physical server seizure does durable damage; paper actions do not
findings.evidence: Zservers (127 servers): near-kill; Stark: sanctions evaded instantly, but 800-server FIOD seizure produced first real friction; Hydra stayed dead after BKA seizure
findings.implication: Target the physical layer in cooperative jurisdictions (NL, DE) where BPH keeps hardware

findings.finding: Trust destruction kills brands faster than takedowns
findings.evidence: ALPHV: dead ~10 weeks after seizure via exit scam; Black Basta: dead on chat leak with zero LE action; XSS: honeypot suspicion collapsed engagement despite 1-day mirror
findings.implication: Information operations against internal trust (leaks, doxxing, honeypot doubt) are a high-ROI complement to takedowns

findings.finding: Demand is displaced, not destroyed (market hydraulics)
findings.evidence: Infostealer rotation RedLine>Lumma>Vidar/StealC (StealC now hit Jun 2026); ALPHV affiliates > RansomHub > Qilin; BPH clients migrate between providers
findings.implication: Plan for the beneficiary: pre-position collection on the likely absorber before the takedown

findings.finding: Payments falling while victim counts hit records
findings.implication: Disruption is fragmenting the market into more, smaller, less profitable groups; payment-side metrics are the honest success measure

findings.finding: Russian safe harbor is the binding constraint
findings.evidence: Khoroshev, Nefedov, Gallyamov, Yakubets, DanaBot 16 all at large in Russia; REvil convictions ended in time-served releases; Cryptex is the lone exception (harmed Russian interests)
findings.implication: Custody leverage exists only at the edges: Western affiliates (UK cluster), travel (Besciokov in India, Panev in Israel, Phuket four), and Russian self-interest

findings.finding: Reconstitution speed is inversely related to personnel exposure
findings.evidence: Financial infra with untouched staff: 1-14 days; malware with indicted-but-free devs: months to never (DanaBot); operations with admins in custody: no reconstitution (Phobos, Cryptex, AudiA6 so far)
findings.implication: Score future operations ex ante by their personnel-exposure component

findings.finding: Top-of-market groups have zero enforcement exposure
findings.evidence: Qilin: #1 in 2025 (958 victims) and all of 2026 to date, no sanctions/indictments/takedowns; Akira #2 (735), same; DragonForce core untouched; streak intact through Jul 2026 while Q2 attack volume runs +30% YoY; analysts publicly flag Qilin as the likely next target
findings.implication: The scoreboard largest gap: the current market leaders are unscored because they have never been hit

findings.finding: Enforcement is shifting to the enabler layer
findings.evidence: Jul 2026 wave: first crypter-vendor designation (Silayev), VPN provider (FirstVPN), MaaS operators personally named (Lumma trio), BPH operators indicted with $10M bounty (Media Land). Personnel exposure now applied to the supply chain, not just brands
findings.implication: Enabler-layer actions raise costs across many groups at once; effectiveness depends on pairing designations with custody, per Findings 1-2. Watch the Media Land window as the test case

gaps.status: Most active RaaS of 2025-2026 (500+ victims in 2026); leading enforcement gap; cartel with LockBit 5.0 and DragonForce
